newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: UNION THREATENS ACTION OVER GOVERNMENT RESTRUCTURE PLANS
The Public Sector Union says industrial action threatens if the Federal Government maintains its current plans to restructure employment in the public service.
Workplace meetings of PSU members will be asked over the next few weeks to consider a stopwork meeting planned for April the 24th to discuss possible industrial action.
Union Secretary Wendy Caird says proposals to abandon across-the-board employment conditions, change classification structures and remove pay increments go against previous government commitments.
ECSTACY FOUND IN COMPACT DISC CARTON
Custom officers in Sydney have seized over seven kilograms of ecstacy in a carton of compact discs.
They say the 25,000 esctacy tablets were concealed in an air cargo bag from the Netherlands.
The Australian Federal Police have charged a 21-year-old women from Pyrmont in connection with the drug importation.
LONG FIELD FOR SHORT'S SENATE POSITION
At least 15 Victorian Liberals are vying to fill the Senate vacancy left by the departure of Jim Short.
The former Assistant Treasurer will resign next month, to take up a banking job in London.
The President of the Victorian Liberal Party, Ted Baillieu, says a good field has already lined up for the Senate pre-selection ballot on April the 20th.
Mr Baillieu, who steps down tomorrow after a five-year stint as President, won't say whether he's among the candidates.
CIRCUSES SAY RSPCA HAS NO EVIDENCE ON ANIMAL SUFFERING
The Circus Federation of Australasia says the RSPCA has ignored evidence from one its own reports in claiming circus animals suffer severe psychological damage.
The federation's executive officer, Mike Mellare says there is no evidence to support the RSPCA's claim and has accused the RSPCA of running a publicity stunt.
Mr Mellare says the report, by a leading animal behaviour expert, concluded circuses do not cause distress and the animals' needs are not served by diverting money to try to ban circuses or zoos.
The RSPCA's campaign is aimed at encouraging the public to pressure local councils to ban circuses with wild animals from performing on council property.
TAX SYSTEM OVERHAUL A KEY POLICY OF HANSON PARTY
Federal Independent, Pauline Hanson, has foreshadowed an overhaul of the tax system as a key policy of her newly-formed political party - One Nation.
At a meeting in the south-east Queensland town of Hervey Bay last night, Ms Hanson added crime, drug rackets, unemployment benefits and politicians' entitlements to her usual list of issues.
She says although she's only recently registered the name of her political party it won't be too long before she's looking for candidates.
